note.note:
History:
• 35-year-old man presents with 3.5-month history of markedly reduced appetite, low energy, and feeling “down.”  
• Unintentional weight loss ≈1 stone (~6 kg) over the past ~6 months.  
• Occasional nausea without vomiting; no specific food triggers.  
• Episodic palpitations and sensation of not getting air when riding in elevators; no chest pain; able to walk ~1 mile without dyspnoea (although currently sedentary).  
• Headaches at work; wife notes decreased libido/“nightly activities.”  
• Bowel habits unchanged: no diarrhoea, blood, mucus, or pain.  
• No cough, reflux, or chest pain.  
• Symptoms began after changing to new law firm (possible stressor).

Past Medical History:
• Primary hypothyroidism (“underactive thyroid”).  
• No surgeries, hospitalisations, or other chronic illnesses recorded.  
• Allergies: Not recorded.  
• Medications: Previously levothyroxine; patient stopped “since I changed doctor” (dose/route/frequency not documented). No current regular medications noted.  
• Family, social, and substance history: Not recorded beyond occupation (lawyer).

Physical Examination:
• Tele-visit; no vitals or physical exam performed.  
• Patient reports: no overt chest pain, no exertional dyspnoea, bowels normal, alert and interactive on call.  
• Additional findings: Not recorded.

Impression:
Unexplained fatigue, appetite loss, and weight loss with episodic palpitations. Working diagnoses:  
1. Relapsed/undertreated hypothyroidism (stopped levothyroxine).  
2. Major depressive disorder ± situational anxiety (low mood, anhedonia, stress at new job).  
3. Anaemia or other systemic cause (to be screened by blood tests).  
DDx list consistent with transcript; no conflicts noted.

Management Plan:
• Order comprehensive blood panel: CBC, renal & liver function, thyroid profile (TSH, free T4), vitamin B12/folate, ferritin, fasting glucose ± HbA1c.  
• Arrange blood draw via support line (patient instructed to call number in app); clinician to complete laboratory requisition form.  
• Follow-up tele-appointment when results available to review findings and consider physical examination or further investigations.  
• Safety-netting: If new chest pain, persistent vomiting, or change in bowel habit occurs, proceed to emergency department (A&E) and/or contact service urgently.  
• Reinforce resumption of thyroid medication only after review of bloods (not started during call).  
• Encourage gradual return to light activity as tolerated; monitor symptoms.  
• Offer reassessment for mood if low mood persists after medical causes evaluated; consider PHQ-9 at next visit.

Patient Summary:
35-year-old man with underactive thyroid (off treatment) now experiencing 3–6 months of appetite loss, fatigue, weight loss, and situational palpitations. Initial evaluation focuses on laboratory work-up (incl. thyroid function and anaemia screen) before physical exam. Safety advice provided.

Key Takeaways:
• Arrange and complete ordered blood tests promptly.  
• Seek urgent care if chest pain, vomiting, or bowel changes develop.  
• Expect a text to schedule follow-up once results are back; do not wait if feeling worse.

Next Steps:
• Patient to telephone support (number in app) to book blood draw.  
• Clinician to review labs; schedule follow-up tele-visit.  
• Depending on results, consider restarting levothyroxine, further imaging, or mental-health referral.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: allergies, detailed medication list (dose/route), vitals, family history, social habits (smoking/alcohol), systems review.  
• Transcript vs DDx conflicts: None identified.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional overlaps but key clinical data audible.
